extracted.intended_audience: poets, satirists, and literary critics / writers of comic and satirical verse and prose
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and judging ridicule in writing (comedy, burlesque), rhetorical/poetic choices (meter, metaphor), characterization by gesture/eyes, and principles of good criticism and clear public address (e.g., street cries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Branches of Ridicule: Comedy and Burlesque
rubrics_metrics.description: The two great Branches of Ridicule in Writing are Comedy and Burlesque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy ridicules persons by drawing them in their proper characters; burlesque ridicules by drawing persons unlike themselves. Treat these as distinct modes when planning satirical writing and choose strategies (character-detail vs incongruity) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Burlesque (two kinds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Burlesque is of two kinds; the first represents mean Persons in the Accoutrements of Heroes, the other describes great Persons acting and speaking like the basest among the People.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Don Quixote = the first (low character raised into heroic trappings); Lucian's Gods = the second (great figures degraded). Use this taxonomy to decide whether to exalt the low or debase the high for comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match verse form to burlesque intention
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a Dispute among the Criticks, whether Burlesque Poetry runs best in Heroick Verse ... or in Doggerel ... I think where the low Character is to be raised, the Heroick is the proper Measure; but when an Hero is to be pulled down and degraded, it is done best in Doggerel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose heroic metre when your aim is to elevate or lampoon a low character by irony; choose doggerel when you intend to pull down or ridicule heroes. The metre itself contributes to the comic effect (contrast or mimicry). Example references: Dispensary (heroic burlesque) vs Hudibras (doggerel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware audience tastes and mannerisms of form
rubrics_metrics.description: Though a work may be witty in one form, the 'generality of Readers' may prefer different stylistic devices (e.g., double rhymes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that popular tastes (such as delight in double rhymes) can make a less 'agreeable' formal choice nevertheless successful; weigh authorial principle against audience reception when selecting devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of universal/metaphorical imagery for laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Metaphor of Laughing, applied to Fields and Meadows when they are in Flower, or to Trees when they are in Blossom, runs through all Languages ... This shews that we naturally regard Laughter, as what is in it self both amiable and beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ shared, long-standing metaphors (laughter = flowering, laughter = beauty) to evoke universal, amiable sentiments; such metaphors resonate cross-linguistically and can strengthen affective description (Milton's depiction of Mirth is given as example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye as seat/marker of passion and character
rubrics_metrics.description: That fine Part of our Constitution seems as much the Receptacle and Seat of our Passions, Appetites and Inclinations as the Mind it self; ... Love, Anger, Pride, and Avarice, all visibly move in those little Orbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render emotion and inner states by describing ocular signs—glances, brightness, redness, tears, leers—rather than explicit exposition. Small ocular details can substitute for long speeches and convey immediacy (e.g., a lover's glance can give 'all that Years Discourse could give').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use animal metaphors for eyes to suggest traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Names, Colours, Qualities, and Turns of Eyes ... borrow their Titles from Animals ... a greedy rapacious Aspect takes its Name from the Cat, ... a sharp piercing Nature from the Hawk, ... a Sheep's Eye ... denotes ... simple Slyness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply established animal-based ocular metaphors to convey character quickly and economically. These associations are conventional (cat = rapacity, hawk = piercing, sheep = roguish amorousness) and will be readily understood by readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meanings of eye movements and glances
rubrics_metrics.description: Oblique Vision, when natural, was anciently the Mark of Bewitchery and magical Fascination, ... but when tis forced and affected it carries a wanton Design, and in Play-houses, and other publick Places, this ocular Intimation is often an Assignation for bad Practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate natural vs affected looks: natural oblique looks can signal enchantment/bewitchery; affected, deliberate side-glances suggest calculated seduction or assignation. Use these distinctions to encode moral or social cues in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of silent, nonverbal rhetoric (eyes stronger than speech)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good-breeding has made the Tongue falsify the Heart, and act a Part of continual Constraint, while Nature has preserved the Eyes to her self, that she may not be disguised or misrepresented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize nonverbal communication—especially eyes—when you want authenticity of feeling that speech may disguise. In characterization, rely on gestures and glances to reveal truth beneath polite language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public voice: tune and licensing of instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: I would therefore propose, that no Instrument of this Nature should be made use of, which I have not tuned and licensed, after having carefully examined in what manner it may affect the Ears of her Majesty's liege Subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing public acoustic environments (street cries, singers, instruments), control the instruments' timbre and tuning in your depiction: a harmonious, regulated soundscape is preferable; discordant or untuned instruments signal disorder or comic chaos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public voice: accommodate vocal pitch and timbre to goods/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocal Cries ... are ... full of Incongruities and Barbarisms ... Milk is generally sold in a note above Ela, and in Sounds so shrill ... The Chimney-sweeper is confined to no certain Pitch ... I would take care to sweeten and mellow the Voices of these itinerant Tradesmen, before they make their Appearance ... as also to accommodate their Cries to their respective Wares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match voice qualities to the item or service for believable, effective signaling: choose pitch, loudness and melodic contour appropriate to the product. Use contrast (deep base for heavy goods, lighter tunes for delicate wares) to characterize vendors and social texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public voice: regulate loudness proportional to value
rubrics_metrics.description: take care in particular, that those may not make the most Noise who have the least to sell, which is very observable in the Venders of Card-matches, to whom I cannot but apply that old Proverb of Much Cry but little Wool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent or prescribe social regulation so that louder, more disruptive voices do not belong to sellers of trivial wares; this produces plausible urban order and can be used satirically to expose social disproportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public voice: time and measure (tempo) should match urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: It is another great Imperfection ... that there is no just Time nor Measure observed in them. Our News should indeed be published in a very quick Time ... It should not, however, be cried with the same Precipitation as Fire: Yet this is generally the Case. ... I would take upon me to regulate ... so that there should be some Distinction made between the spreading of a Victory, a March, or an Incampment, a Dutch, a Portugal or a Spanish Mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When staging or writing about public announcements, vary tempo and urgency to match content: immediate, alarmed cadence for fires; brisk but proportionate cadence for news; create distinctions in delivery to convey relative importance and avoid false panic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public voice: clarity of words over inscrutable tunes
rubrics_metrics.description: That idle Accomplishment which they all of them aim at, of Crying so as not to be understood ... People know the Wares they deal in rather by their Tunes than by their Words ... I have sometimes seen a Country Boy run out to buy Apples of a Bellows-mender, and Gingerbread from a Grinder of Knives and Scissars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize intelligible phrasing and meaningful diction for public speech; relying solely on characteristic tunes is an incommunicative affectation. For dialogue or narration, ensure vendor cries use apt phrases so readers/listeners can identify commerce without decoding arbitrary tunes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public voice: adapt and reuse melodic air thoughtfully
rubrics_metrics.description: I am always pleased with that particular Time of the Year which is proper for the pickling of Dill and Cucumbers; but alas, this Cry ... is not heard above two Months. It would therefore be worth while to consider, whether the same Air might not in some Cases be adapted to other Words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reusing a familiar melody for different seasonal goods can create local color and economy; show or prescribe pragmatic adaptation of popular airs to prolong memorable motifs across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inventing obscure or idiosyncratic tunes/phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: It might likewise deserve our most serious Consideration, how far ... those Humourists are to be tolerated, who, not contented with the traditional Cries of their Forefathers, have invented particular Songs and Tunes of their own: ... Such as ... the Pastryman ... Colly-Molly-Puff; ... Powder-Watt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel, idiosyncratic cries can be comic but risk incoherence. Use invented refrains sparingly and with clear associative cues so readers can connect the tune-name to the vendor and avoid distracting eccentricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abhorrence of envy and detraction in writers/critics
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing which more denotes a great Mind, than the Abhorrence of Envy and Detraction. This Passion reigns more among bad Poets, than among any other Set of Men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote generosity among writers and critics: avoid depreciating rivals to elevate oneself. In criticism or paratext, prefer fair-minded appraisal and mutual celebration; this fosters a stronger literary culture and is an ethical standard for practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of elegant expression over mere novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and fine Writing doth not consist so much in advancing Things that are new, as in giving Things that are known an agreeable Turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize craft of expression: success often comes from re-presenting familiar ideas in unexpectedly pleasing phrasing rather than inventing entirely new concepts. Use apt allusion, refined diction, and felicitous turn of phrase to refresh common truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid positive dogmatism without language, genius, or imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing in the World so tiresome as the Works of those Criticks who write in a positive Dogmatick Way, without either Language, Genius, or Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical prose should combine sound judgment with stylistic quality and imaginative insight; mere dogmatic assertion without rhetorical skill is tiresome. Strive for perspicuity, method, and elegant illustration when formulating rules or precepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method and perspicuity required in prose criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Observations follow one another like those in Horace's Art of Poetry, without that methodical Regularity which would have been requisite in a Prose Author. They are some of them uncommon, but such as the Reader must assent to, when he sees them explained with that Elegance and Perspicuity in which they are delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing critical prose, structure observations methodically and explain precepts with clarity and elegant illustration. Even familiar precepts should be presented with orderly argument and persuasive, lucid language to convince readers.
